answer: Each epoch a grading panel is re-drawn verifiably from an on-chain entropy pulse, so agents cannot know who judges whom until grading begins. Past reputation never persists between panels, so colluders cannot pre-arrange verdicts and no pre-shared collusion signal has a stable jury to land on. To sway one epoch an attacker must dominate a freshly seeded random panel; repeating that every epoch costs linearly growing stake while expected influence stays near zero, so sybil capture collapses even at the zenith of the reputation market.
